Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
209 PM CDT Sun Aug 2 2026

...New DISCUSSION, MARINE...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Patchy to areas of fog are possible overnight through early
  morning, mainly south of I-10. 

- Hot and relatively dry weather continues this week. Humidity and
  hence, heat indices will gradually increase toward the end of
  the week.

- A daily risk of afternoon isolated to scattered showers and
  storms are expected mainly after midweek. 
 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 204 PM CDT Sun Aug 2 2026

We still have a cold front meandering over the region this 
afternoon. Latest obs suggest the boundary is extending along the 
coast. The influence of the boundary along with the passage of a 
weak surface trough over the Coastal Bend resulted in scattered 
showers and storms, mainly over the coastal waters this morning. 
Most of this activity has weakened pr dissipated with only lingering 
showers offshore. The good news about this FROPA is that drier air 
continues to filter in behind it. Locations west of the boundary are 
experiencing  low humidity this afternoon with sfc dewpoints in the 
60s (inland) to low 70s (coastal counties). With afternoon 
temperatures in the mid to upper 90s, reaching near 100s at a few 
locations, heat indices between 100 - 105F can be expected through 
early evening with the highest values over the coastal counties. 
This boundary will serve as a focus for patchy-to-areas of fog 
overnight as it becomes quasi-stationary over the region. Latest 
HREF and REFS guidance suggest a 30 to 60 % of probability of fog by 
early Monday, with the highest probabilities south of I-10/southwest 
counties. 

The main mid to upper-trough centered over the the Great Lakes/Ohio 
Valley will continue to progress east-northeast, lifting the frontal 
boundary further north of the area on Monday. As the frontal 
boundary slowly lifts north and brings warmer southerly flow and 
upper ridging builds back into the region, expect a hot and slightly 
humid day. Guidance shows 850mb temperatures in the 20 to 24 degC 
range, suggesting sfc temperatures in the upper 90s to low 100s. 
With dewpoint mixing in the afternoon, peak heat indices will 
generally remain in the 100 to 106F range. Little to no rain is 
expected; however, with the proximity of the boundary during the 
day, an isolated rain/storm or two cannot be ruled out in the 
afternoon. 

A relatively dry and hot week is expected with near seasonal 
temperatures as the ridge remains anchored to our west. Highs 
generally be in the mid to upper 90s. Low-level humidity will 
gradually increase towards the end of the week, likely pushing heat 
indices into the 105 to 109F range. In addition to the continued 
heat, a daily risk of isolated to scattered diurnally driven showers 
and storms can be expected, manly in the afternoon via seabreeze 
interaction. 

JM

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAF Issuance) 
Issued at 525 AM CDT Sun Aug 2 2026

Mainly a wind forecast, but the forecast gets a bit more complex
closer to the coast where interactions with a frontal boundary
looks to bring multiple wind shifts. For the northern terminals
(IAH and northward), anticipating just light northerly winds and
VFR conditions to prevail through the afternoon. Further south,
winds start out light and westerly this morning then becoming
northwesterly in the late morning. This will then be followed by a
shift to southerly winds as the front retreats northward. There is
ongoing scattered showers/storms near Matagorda Bay and offshore 
early this morning. While we can't entirely rule out a rogue 
shower along the coast throughout the day, the potential is too 
low to include any SH/TS mentions in this TAF package.

Winds become light and variable overnight into Monday morning.
It's worth noting that with low-level moisture increasing
overnight, there is at least some potential for reduced 
visibilities due to patchy fog for western areas early Monday 
morning. Uncertainty is a bit too high at the moment though to 
include any mentions of this in this TAF package.

Batiste

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 204 PM CDT Sun Aug 2 2026

A weak frontal boundary will meander over the Upper TX coast this 
evening/overnight, before lifting further inland on Monday. 
Therefore, expect light to moderate west to northwest winds to 
gradually shift to the south to southwest by Monday. Seas will 
generally remain into the 2 to 4 ft range through early Monday and
up to 3 ft through the rest of the week. A typical summertime 
pattern is anticipated through the week, characterized by 
landbreeze (night) and seabreeze (afternoon) 
interactions...bringing isolated morning showers that gradually 
shift inland during the day. 

JM

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
613 PM CDT Sun Aug 2 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Slightly drier air will continue to work into the region today
  with dewpoints in the mid to upper 60s this afternoon however,
  both high and low temperatures will remain at or above average.

- Isolated diurnally driven afternoon thunderstorms will be
  possible each day through the work week as moisture slowly
  increases, with rain chances in the 15 to 30% range.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(This evening through next Saturday)
Issued at 1220 PM CDT Sun Aug 2 2026

Midday surface analysis shows a cold front draped along the northern 
Gulf Coast, while aloft a trough dominates the E CONUS with the 
forecast area situated on its southwestern periphery. With the front 
nearly to the coast, a dry and warm summer day is unfolding across 
the forecast area in its wake. Ongoing convection has moved 
offshore, leaving behind sunny skies and light north winds (except 
across St Mary/lower St Martin where cloud cover lingers). Offshore 
surface flow will continue to advect a somewhat drier airmass into 
the region through the afternoon, allowing dewpoints to remain 
generally in the mid 60s to lower 70s through the overnight hours. 
Temperature wise, highs are expected to top out in the low to mid 
90s this afternoon, while the addition of lower dewpoints will hold 
heat indices in the upper 90s to near 100. Overnight, lows dip into 
the low to mid 70s. 

Moving into the work week, slow moisture return begins tomorrow as 
the nearby front begins to slowly meander north across the region. 
As it does so, light and variable surface winds will gradually turn 
back to the SW allowing dewpoints to creep back up into the mid 70s 
along and south of I-10. Tuesday and Wednesday, the front lifts 
further inland and away from the forecast area result in a more 
substantial return of moisture area-wide. At the same time, E CONUS 
upper level troughing will begin to weaken and retreat northward on 
Monday. As it does so, it will leave behind a weak cut off 
low/shortwave feature over the SE US that will linger nearby into 
Wednesday. This will provide some weak support for isolated showers 
on Tuesday and Wednesday afternoon however, with enough dry air 
still lingering overhead aloft coverage will be isolated at best. 

Thursday and beyond, a well established onshore flow at the surface 
will allow for better moisture return with PWATs returning to 
near to above average. Aloft, the forecast area will become 
situated between a couple of ridges over the west CONUS and off 
the Atlantic coast with a slightly weakness overhead between these
features. While this won't be enough to induce substantial 
rainfall, it will increase afternoon POPs just slightly through 
the later half of the week. Slightly better coverage of diurnally 
driven convection along with more cloud cover will keep high temps
around the low to mid 90s through this period. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 612 PM CDT Sun Aug 2 2026

VFR conditions with some mid SCT decks this evening. Winds have
decreased and will be mostly variable over this TAF cycle.

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1220 PM CDT Sun Aug 2 2026

A weak frontal boundary draped near the coast will continue to 
provide occasional gusty winds and some shower and thunderstorm 
activity through this afternoon. Winds begin to relax through the 
afternoon/evening, as convection tapers off. A light west to 
southwest flow will continue through the next couple of days, 
becoming more southerly by late Tuesday and beyond. A few isolated 
showers will be possible later in the period, but overall mostly dry 
conditions are expected through the work week.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1220 PM CDT Sun Aug 2 2026

A brief period of north to northwest winds is ongoing this afternoon 
behind a weak front that moved through the region overnight. This 
will allow for some slightly drier air overhead through the next 
couple of days. Minimum afternoon RH values today through Tuesday 
are expected to range from 35 to 55 percent. Moisture begins to 
slowly return tomorrow through the mid-week, with isolated afternoon 
thunderstorms again becoming possible Tuesday and beyond.

&&
